name: The Midnight Library
author: Matt Haig
synopsis: This novel centers on Nora Seed, a woman overwhelmed by regret and convinced her life is meaningless. At the moment she decides to end her life, she finds herself in the Midnight Library, a place between life and death. The library's shelves are filled with books, each one offering her the chance to live out an alternate version of her life based on different choices she could have made. Guided by the librarian, Mrs. Elm, Nora begins to try on these other lives—a life as a rock star, a glaciologist, a pub owner, and more—in a quest to find a life she truly wants to live. Ultimately, her journey through her infinite potential lives forces her to confront what truly constitutes a happy and fulfilling existence.

name: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
synopsis: Set in a distant future feudal galactic empire, Dune follows the young nobleman Paul Atreides, whose family is given stewardship of the desert planet Arrakis. Arrakis is the universe's only source of the spice, a priceless substance that extends life and enhances mental abilities, making it crucial for space navigation. When House Atreides is betrayed by its enemies, Paul and his mother escape into the desert and are taken in by the Fremen, the planet's native inhabitants. There, Paul grapples with his destiny as a prophesied messiah, honing his latent powers to lead the Fremen in a rebellion that will change the fate of the entire universe. The story is a complex tapestry of politics, religion, ecology, and human potential.

name: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
synopsis: Narrated by a young girl named Scout Finch, this novel is set in the racially charged atmosphere of Maycomb, Alabama, during the 1930s. The story follows Scout, her brother Jem, and their widowed father, Atticus Finch, a principled lawyer. The core of the plot revolves around Atticus's decision to defend Tom Robinson, a black man falsely accused of raping a white woman. Through Scout's innocent yet perceptive eyes, the reader witnesses the deep-seated prejudice and hypocrisy of the town's adult world. The children's loss of innocence is mirrored by the town's struggle with justice and morality, making the novel a powerful exploration of racial injustice, courage, and compassion.

author: George Orwell
synopsis: George Orwells dystopian masterpiece is set in Oceania, a totalitarian superstate where the ruling Party, led by the enigmatic Big Brother, exercises absolute control. The protagonist, Winston Smith, works in the Ministry of Truth, altering historical records to match the Party's ever-changing propaganda. Secretly hating the oppressive regime and its constant surveillance through telescreens, Winston begins a forbidden act of rebellion by keeping a diary and starting a secret affair with a colleague named Julia. His journey is a harrowing exploration of psychological manipulation, the nature of truth, and the fight for individuality in a world where even independent thought (thoughtcrime) is a punishable offense.

name: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
synopsis: Told from the perspective of Nick Carraway, this novel explores the glitz and moral decay of the Roaring Twenties on Long Island. Nick moves next door to the mysterious and fabulously wealthy Jay Gatsby, who throws extravagant parties every weekend. Nick soon learns that Gatsby's entire opulent lifestyle is an elaborate scheme to win back the love of his life, Daisy Buchanan, who is now married to the brutish and wealthy Tom Buchanan. As Nick is drawn into their world of secrets, obsession, and tragedy, the novel serves as a poignant critique of the American Dream, the illusion of wealth, and the impossibility of recreating the past.

name: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
image: assets/images/Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone.jpg
author: J.K. Rowling
synopsis: This is the story of Harry Potter, an orphan who believes he is an ordinary boy living a miserable life with his cruel relatives, the Dursleys. On his eleventh birthday, his world is turned upside down when he learns he is a wizard and has been accepted into Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. At Hogwarts, Harry discovers the truth about his parents' deaths at the hands of the dark wizard Lord Voldemort and finds he is famous in the wizarding world. Alongside his new friends, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger, Harry navigates the challenges of school life while uncovering a plot to steal the Philosopher's Stone, an object that grants immortality, forcing him into a direct confrontation with the forces that murdered his family.

name: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J.D. Salinger
synopsis: The novel is a first-person narrative told by Holden Caulfield, a cynical and disillusioned sixteen-year-old who has just been expelled from his fourth prep school. Over the course of a few days, Holden wanders through New York City, interacting with a variety of characters and reflecting on his life. He is deeply critical of the phoniness he perceives in the adult world and is tormented by feelings of alienation, grief over his younger brother's death, and the painful transition into adulthood. The book is a seminal work on teenage angst and rebellion, capturing the search for identity and authenticity in a world that seems corrupt and superficial.

name: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
synopsis: Set in early 19th-century England, this classic novel of manners follows the Bennet family and their five unmarried daughters. The story primarily focuses on the witty and independent Elizabeth Bennet and her turbulent relationship with the wealthy, proud, and socially aloof Mr. Fitzwilliam Darcy. Their initial encounters are marred by his snobbery and her sharp-tongued prejudice against him. Through a series of social events, misunderstandings, and personal revelations, both characters are forced to confront their own biases and flaws. The novel is a masterful and satirical exploration of class, reputation, love, and marriage in Georgian society.

name: The Hobbit
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
synopsis: The Hobbit is the tale of Bilbo Baggins, a respectable, comfort-loving hobbit whose peaceful life is interrupted when the wizard Gandalf and a company of thirteen dwarves arrive at his door. They recruit him as their burglar on a grand adventure to reclaim their stolen treasure from Smaug, a fearsome dragon living in the Lonely Mountain. Pushed far outside his comfort zone, Bilbo encounters trolls, goblins, giant spiders, and other dangers. Along the way, he discovers a magical ring of invisibility and uncovers a reserve of courage and resourcefulness he never knew he possessed, transforming from a simple homebody into a true hero.

name: The Da Vinci Code
author: Dan Brown
synopsis: Harvard symbologist Robert Langdon is awakened in his Paris hotel room and summoned to the Louvre Museum, where a curator has been murdered, leaving behind a series of baffling symbols and clues. Teaming up with Sophie Neveu, a gifted French cryptologist and the victim's granddaughter, Langdon is plunged into a thrilling, high-stakes hunt. They discover that the clues are hidden within the works of Leonardo da Vinci and point to a secret society that has guarded a historical conspiracy for centuries—one that could shatter the very foundations of Western history. The pair must decipher the riddles while being pursued by both the police and a ruthless agent of a shadowy religious organization.

name: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
synopsis: This allegorical novel tells the story of Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd boy who has a recurring dream about a treasure hidden at the base of the Egyptian pyramids. Interpreting this as his destiny, or Personal Legend, he sells his flock and embarks on a long and transformative journey across North Africa. Along the way, he meets a series of spiritual guides, including a mysterious old king and an alchemist, who teach him to listen to his heart, read the omens of the universe, and pursue his dreams against all odds. The book is a philosophical fable about the importance of following one's path and finding meaning in the journey itself.

name: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
synopsis: Aldous Huxleys dystopian novel presents a futuristic World State where society is built on scientific principles of control and conditioning. Citizens are genetically engineered into a rigid caste system, pacified with a pleasure drug called soma, and conditioned to embrace promiscuity and consumerism. The story follows Bernard Marx, an Alpha-caste member who feels like an outcast, and John, a Savage raised outside this society on a reservation with Shakespearean values. When Bernard brings John to the civilized world, John's ideals of love, freedom, and individuality clash violently with the hedonistic and emotionless society, leading to a tragic confrontation about the price of happiness and the meaning of humanity.

name: The Hunger Games
author: Suzanne Collins
synopsis: In the dystopian nation of Panem, the wealthy Capitol maintains control over twelve impoverished districts by forcing each to send a boy and a girl to participate in the annual Hunger Games—a brutal, televised fight to the death. The story follows sixteen-year-old Katniss Everdeen, who volunteers to take her younger sister's place in the games. A skilled hunter, Katniss must rely on her instincts and survival skills to navigate the deadly arena and the complex political machinations of the games. As she becomes a reluctant symbol of hope and rebellion for the oppressed districts, her actions spark a fire that threatens to consume the tyrannical regime.

name: The Shining
author: Stephen King
synopsis: Jack Torrance, a struggling writer and recovering alcoholic, accepts a job as the winter caretaker at the remote and snowbound Overlook Hotel in the Colorado Rockies, bringing his wife, Wendy, and their five-year-old son, Danny. Danny possesses a psychic ability known as the shining, which makes him sensitive to the hotel's malevolent supernatural history. As the winter isolation sets in, the hotel's dark forces prey on Jack's weaknesses, driving him into a spiral of insanity and violence. The story becomes a terrifying struggle for survival as Wendy and Danny must fight against the man who was supposed to protect them.

name: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
image: assets/images/The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo.jpg
author: Stieg Larsson
synopsis: This Swedish crime thriller introduces two protagonists: Mikael Blomkvist, a crusading journalist recently disgraced by a libel conviction, and Lisbeth Salander, a brilliant but deeply antisocial computer hacker with a traumatic past. Blomkvist is hired by an aging industrialist to investigate the 40-year-old disappearance of his great-niece from a remote island. As Blomkvist digs into the powerful family's dark secrets, his path crosses with Salander's. Together, the unlikely pair uncovers a horrifying trail of misogyny, corruption, and murder, while Salander concurrently wages her own brutal war for justice against the men who have wronged her.

name: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
image: assets/images/The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.jpg
author: Douglas Adams
synopsis: This wildly imaginative and satirical science fiction novel begins moments before the Earth is demolished to make way for a hyperspace bypass. The unassuming Englishman Arthur Dent is saved at the last second by his friend, Ford Prefect, who reveals he is an alien researcher for The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, a travel guide that offers advice like Don't Panic. What follows is a bizarre and hilarious adventure through space with a cast of eccentric characters, including the two-headed, ego-driven Galactic President Zaphod Beeblebrox and a perpetually depressed robot named Marvin. The story is a brilliant parody of bureaucracy, philosophy, and the search for the meaning of life, which, according to a supercomputer, is simply 42.

name: The Kite Runner
author: Khaled Hosseini
synopsis: Set in Afghanistan, this powerful and emotional novel tells the story of Amir, a young boy from a wealthy family in Kabul, and his close friendship with Hassan, the son of his father's Hazara servant. Their bond is shattered by a traumatic event during a kite-fighting tournament, where Amir's act of cowardice and subsequent betrayal haunts him for the rest of his life. Years later, after fleeing to America, an adult Amir is given a chance at redemption. He must return to his war-torn homeland, now under Taliban rule, to confront his past and rescue the son of his estranged friend, on a dangerous journey to find a way to be good again.

name: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
synopsis: This fantasy novel is presented as the first day of an autobiography told by Kvothe, a legendary hero who is now living in hiding as a humble innkeeper. When a chronicler discovers him, Kvothe agrees to tell the true story of his life. He recounts his childhood as a member of a troupe of traveling performers, the devastating tragedy that left him an orphan, and his years surviving as a clever street urchin in a dangerous city. The bulk of the story follows his journey to the prestigious University, where he studies magic, music, and science, all while relentlessly seeking knowledge about the Chandrian, the mysterious and mythical beings responsible for his family's murder.

name: The Handmaid's Tale
author: Margaret Atwood
synopsis: This sprawling historical epic is set in 12th-century England during a time of civil war and instability known as The Anarchy. The novel's central thread is the decades-long construction of a magnificent Gothic cathedral in the fictional town of Kingsbridge. The story follows the intertwined lives and ambitions of a diverse cast of characters: the dedicated Prior Philip, the visionary master builder Tom, the resilient and wronged noblewoman Aliena, and her nemesis, the cruel William Hamleigh. Their personal dramas of love, betrayal, and faith are set against a rich backdrop of political intrigue and social change, with the cathedral serving as a symbol of hope and human aspiration.

name: The Fault in Our Stars
author: John Green
synopsis: This gripping science fiction novel follows astronaut Mark Watney, who is presumed dead and left behind by his crew after a fierce storm on Mars. Armed with only his ingenuity, his scientific expertise, and an unwavering sense of humor, Watney must figure out how to survive alone on a hostile planet with limited resources. The story alternates between Watneys clever, problem-solving log entries as he figures out how to grow food, create water, and establish communication, and the monumental efforts of NASA scientists on Earth who, upon discovering he is alive, launch an audacious and seemingly impossible mission to bring him home. It is a thrilling tribute to human resilience and the power of science.

name: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
image: assets/images/Sapiens A Brief History of Humankind.jpg
author: Yuval Noah Harari
synopsis: Set in the Republic of Gilead, a totalitarian and theocratic state that has replaced the United States, this dystopian novel explores a society where birthrates have plummeted. Fertile women are stripped of all rights and forced into sexual servitude as Handmaids for the ruling elite, tasked with bearing children for childless couples. The story is told from the perspective of Offred, a Handmaid assigned to a powerful Commander. Through her eyes, we experience the oppressive daily reality of her life, her memories of the freedom she lost, and her subtle acts of rebellion in a world where surveillance is constant and dissent is fatal.

name: The Lord of the Rings
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
synopsis: This novel tells the poignant and witty story of Hazel Grace Lancaster, a sixteen-year-old girl living with terminal thyroid cancer. At a cancer support group, she meets Augustus Gus Waters, a charismatic and optimistic boy in remission from osteosarcoma. They form an immediate and profound connection, bonding over their experiences and a shared love for a novel about a cancer patient. Their relationship blossoms into a beautiful and heartbreaking love story as they embark on a journey to Amsterdam to meet the book's reclusive author. The novel thoughtfully explores themes of life, love, and mortality, capturing the humor and tragedy of being young and in love while facing death.

name: Becoming
author: Michelle Obama
synopsis: In this sweeping non-fiction work, historian Yuval Noah Harari examines the entire history of the human species, from the emergence of Homo sapiens in the Stone Age to the political and technological revolutions of the 21st century. Harari structures his narrative around three major revolutions: the Cognitive Revolution, the Agricultural Revolution, and the Scientific Revolution. He argues that the key to humanity's success is its unique ability to cooperate in large numbers through a belief in shared fictions, such as gods, nations, money, and human rights. It's a thought-provoking exploration of how our species came to dominate the planet and what that means for our future.

name: One Hundred Years of Solitude
author: Gabriel García Márquez
synopsis: This epic fantasy saga is the story of a humble hobbit named Frodo Baggins, who inherits a magical ring from his uncle Bilbo. He soon discovers it is the One Ring, a powerful and ancient weapon of evil created by the Dark Lord Sauron to enslave Middle-earth. To prevent the world from falling into darkness, Frodo must embark on a perilous quest to the land of Mordor to destroy the Ring in the fires of Mount Doom, the only place it can be unmade. He is aided by a diverse group of companions—the Fellowship of the Ring—in a monumental struggle against overwhelming evil that explores themes of friendship, courage, temptation, and sacrifice.

name: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
synopsis: This is the memoir of Michelle Obama, the former First Lady of the United States. In it, she traces her life's journey, from her childhood growing up on the South Side of Chicago to her years as a successful lawyer and executive, her marriage to Barack Obama, and her transformative time in the White House. With warmth and honesty, she shares personal stories about the challenges of balancing a career and motherhood, the pressures of public life, and her work to create a more inclusive and welcoming nation. The book is an inspiring and intimate reflection on her personal growth, her heritage, and finding one's voice.

name: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J.D. Salinger
synopsis: This non-fiction work investigates the story of Henrietta Lacks, a poor African American tobacco farmer whose cells were taken without her knowledge or consent in 1951. These cells, known as HeLa, became the first immortal human cell line, meaning they could reproduce indefinitely in a lab. They have since become one of the most important tools in modern medicine, vital for developing the polio vaccine, cloning, gene mapping, and countless other scientific breakthroughs. Author Rebecca Skloot masterfully weaves together the scientific history of HeLa with the personal story of Henrietta's family, exploring the profound ethical questions of race, class, and consent in medical research.

name: Educated
author: Tara Westover
synopsis: A landmark work of magical realism, this novel chronicles seven generations of the Buendía family in the mythical, isolated town of Macondo, which they founded. The story is a sprawling, dreamlike tapestry that weaves together history, myth, and fantasy, where supernatural events are treated as ordinary occurrences. It follows the family's cyclical patterns of love, war, obsession, and solitude, as characters with repeating names seem destined to repeat the tragic fates of their ancestors. The novel serves as a powerful allegory for Latin American history, exploring themes of time, memory, and the inescapable loneliness of the human condition.

name: The Pillars of the Earth
author: Ken Follett
synopsis: This psychological thriller centers on Alicia Berenson, a famous painter who brutally murders her husband and then falls into complete silence, refusing to speak a single word. She is committed to a secure psychiatric facility, where her case becomes a source of intense media fascination. Theo Faber, a psychotherapist obsessed with uncovering the truth, takes a job at the facility, determined to get Alicia to talk and unravel the mystery of her violent act. The narrative alternates between Theos investigation in the present and excerpts from Alicias diary leading up to the murder, building suspense towards a shocking twist that changes everything.

name: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
image: assets/images/The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks.jpg
author: Rebecca Skloot

The book is a seminal work on teenage angst and rebellion, capturing the search for identity and authenticity in a world that seems corrupt and superficial.

name: The name of the Wind
author: Patrick Rothfuss
synopsis: This powerful memoir tells the story of Tara Westover, who was raised in a fundamentalist Mormon survivalist family in rural Idaho. Isolated from mainstream society, she and her siblings were forbidden from attending school or visiting doctors. Despite a childhood marked by abuse and a complete lack of formal education, Tara develops a powerful thirst for knowledge. Teaching herself enough to pass the ACT, she gains admission to Brigham Young University and begins a journey that takes her across oceans to study at Cambridge and Harvard. The book is a moving account of her struggle to reconcile her quest for knowledge with her loyalty to a family that sees her education as a betrayal.
